topic.title: How I Keep Iterating Kaggriculture Agents

comments.content: Your openness is appreciated. I can't speak for everyone, but i'm working 2 lanes (and I suspect a lot of others are as well): the first lane clones and then optimizes the current meta, while the second lane builds toward developing new metas. I haven't had any luck developing something new (I genuinely don't know how some people are doing it), but I think I get a little closer every day.

Thank you — I really like the two-lane framing. I may see the boundary between them a little differently, though.

To me, countering the current meta can itself be the process of creating a new meta. If the counter only exploits one specific route, it is probably just a temporary anti-meta. But if it identifies why the current meta works and develops a general response that forces others to adapt, then that response may become the next meta.

So perhaps the real distinction is not optimization versus innovation, but countering a specific implementation versus replacing the principle behind it. In that sense, I think the two lanes are closely connected.

And I completely relate to the difficulty of discovering something genuinely new. Even when an experiment fails, it still feels like one more step toward understanding the game.

Thanks a lot for this. I got in top 10 just because of your notebook but i dont feel good about it bcz its not my work. I'll try your approach and try building better agents and most importantly "my Agents" instead of cloning the next public notebook.

Thank you for sharing this important project. When I first tried to participate, I couldn't understand everything because my study approach was a bit outdated, which was somewhat frustrating. ​When I went back and tried again, I realized where the issues were. That’s why I decided to study more deeply. I agree with you that copying or relying on notebook notes in a competition is great at the beginning, but over time, it won't get you to high ranks or help you win prizes simply because everyone has access to the exact same setup. ​The real question is how to evolve, carve your own path, and stand out. I'm not against using starter notebooks, but you need an edge to reach top-tier levels. I remember in one of the competitions, there was a specific approach I unfortunately discovered too late. If only I had asked myself back then, 'Why are people using this specific method?' when I was reading books. ​Ultimately, learning while sharing building AI applications is a wonderful journey. I'm currently learning it through the book Building Ai Agents for Applications. Thank you again
